title: Mazdutide: Phase 3-Proven GLP-1/Glucagon Dual Agonist — Research Dossier
excerpt: Mazdutide (IBI362) is the most clinically advanced GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist globally, with Phase 3 GLORY data published in NEJM (2025) and 18.6% weight loss at ADA 2026. It is approved in China for obesity and has an extensive multi-indication Phase 3 pipeline including MASH, HFpEF, and adolescent obesity.

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

What Is Mazdutide?

Mazdutide (IBI362, also known as LY3305677) is a once-weekly injectable peptide co-developed by Innovent Biologics and Eli Lilly that simultaneously activates both GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptors and glucagon receptors. It is the most clinically advanced GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist globally, having completed multiple Phase 3 trials with results published in the New England Journal of Medicine (2025) and having received regulatory approval in China for the treatment of obesity in adults.

Mechanism of Action

  • GLP-1 receptor activation: Glucose-dependent insulin secretion, glucagon suppression in the pancreas, slowed gastric emptying, and appetite reduction via central nervous system pathways.
  • Glucagon receptor activation: Drives hepatic fatty acid oxidation, activates thermogenic programs through brown adipose tissue and FGF21, and mobilizes stored liver fat. This component provides energy expenditure ‘on top of’ the appetite-suppression effects of GLP-1, potentially enabling greater total weight loss and superior liver-fat reduction compared to GLP-1 mono-agonism.

The dual mechanism is balanced to avoid net hyperglycemia: GLP-1’s insulin-stimulating effect counterbalances glucagon’s glucose-raising effect, so the net metabolic outcome is improved glycemic control rather than worsening.

Key Research Findings

GLORY-1 Phase 3 Trial (NEJM 2025)

  • Design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial
  • Population: Chinese adults with overweight or obesity
  • Primary dose (6 mg weekly): 12.55% mean body weight reduction
  • Published in New England Journal of Medicine, 2025
  • Primary endpoint met with high statistical significance

GLORY-2 Phase 3 Trial (ADA 2026)

  • Population: 462 Chinese adults with obesity
  • Dose tested: up to 9 mg weekly
  • 18.6% mean sustained body weight reduction
  • 44.0% of participants achieved ≥20% body weight reduction vs. 2.6% on placebo
  • Serious adverse events: 7.2% (mazdutide) vs. 5.2% (placebo)
  • Presented at the American Diabetes Association (ADA) Annual Scientific Sessions 2026

Phase 2 Dose-Finding (ObesityWeek 2025)

  • Dose 16 mg weekly (highest tested): 22.3% weight loss at 48 weeks
  • Weight loss of 18.1% observed at 32 weeks, increasing to 22.3% at 48 weeks (still rising)
  • GI adverse events increased at higher doses

Regulatory Approval (China)

  • The National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) accepted Innovent’s NDA (new drug application) for mazdutide for overweight or obese adults
  • Approved in China based on GLORY Phase 3 data — making it the first GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist with real-world market approval
  • Not approved by the FDA or EMA; investigational outside China

Ongoing Phase 3 Programs (as of October 2026)

  • Adolescent obesity
  • Type 2 diabetes
  • MASH (metabolic-associated steatohepatitis)
  • Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
  • Hypertension
  • Sleep apnea
  • DREAMS-3: head-to-head Phase 3 vs. tirzepatide in Chinese adults with T2D and obesity (ongoing)

Dosing in Research

Phase 3 trials used once-weekly subcutaneous doses of 3 mg, 6 mg, 9 mg, and 16 mg. Phase 3 approval in China was based on specific doses established in the GLORY trials. These are clinical trial doses and do not represent FDA-approved or globally approved dosing regimens outside of China. Outside of China, mazdutide is available only within authorized clinical trials.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is mazdutide approved and available?

Mazdutide is approved in China for the treatment of adults with overweight or obesity, based on Phase 3 GLORY data. It is not FDA-approved or available in the United States outside of clinical trials. It is not approved in the EU. For physicians and patients in China, it represents a commercially available option; for everyone else, it remains investigational.

How does mazdutide compare to tirzepatide for weight loss?

Mazdutide (GLP-1/glucagon) and tirzepatide (GLP-1/GIP) take different dual-receptor approaches. Phase 3 weight loss for mazdutide (18.6% at 9 mg) is broadly comparable to tirzepatide’s Phase 3 data (approximately 20-22% at highest dose). The mechanistic differences — glucagon agonism vs. GIP agonism — may translate to different profiles for liver fat, lean mass, and metabolic comorbidities. A head-to-head DREAMS-3 trial is ongoing in 2026 and will provide direct comparative data.

What other conditions is mazdutide being studied for?

Mazdutide has one of the broadest Phase 3 pipelines of any obesity drug: adolescent obesity, MASH, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), hypertension, sleep apnea, and type 2 diabetes. The HFpEF and hypertension programs are particularly significant given the high co-prevalence of these cardiovascular conditions with obesity — an area where the metabolic and possibly anti-inflammatory effects of GLP-1/glucagon co-agonism may have special relevance.

Research Limitations

  • Phase 3 data published to date are predominantly from Chinese populations; generalizability to non-Asian populations requires ongoing global trials
  • Head-to-head data vs. semaglutide and tirzepatide in non-Asian populations are not yet available
  • Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trial data are not yet available
  • Higher doses (16 mg) have more GI adverse events, and the optimal benefit-risk dose for different populations is not fully established
  • MASH, HFpEF, and other indication-specific Phase 3 data are still being collected
  • FDA approval pathway and timeline are unknown
